title: El Paso 1936-51: Bob Watts and a mixed Mexican band
summary: Williams was in El Paso from 1936 to 1951; he led a mixed band with trumpeter Bob Watts and Mexican musicians who played American music but not New Orleans style, though he taught them tunes.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Well, you would've seen him in San Antone maybe.
No, no. I'm 600 miles from San Antone. Where were you? You were in El Paso.
What years were you there? How long were you there?
I was in El Paso from 36 to 51. From 36 to 51.
All through the war and then the last one. That's right.
I was on that job, that picture that you see on the band. I stayed on that job.
You have any New Orleans guys out there with you? No.

I had one guy. He came out in 46, Bob Watts. What did he play? Trumpet. Most of the time I had a mixed band. Some of the time I had white Mexicans. On the last I had, nobody was in the band. But me, I had four Mexicans with myself for about three years until my job closed.
What kind of music did the Mexicans play? My kind of music. College music. American music. They were, man. They were, man.

They could play American music. American music. American music. Fine musicians. Yeah, fine musicians. Yeah, they played American music. Would they play New Orleans style jazz? No, they couldn't. They couldn't. They tried.
But they did the best they could. All right.
Oh yeah. We made them like it. Oh yeah. We made them like it. Because I learned them. You see, because I learned them a lot about our tunes.
They had very good ears. They knew the music.
And the ears was very good.
And the ears was very good.
And they would come. And after little Bob Watts come out there.
Well, they learned a lot of the tunes.

Because he could play them. You see. He learned a lot of our tunes. Oh yeah. They learned a lot of them. He had a fine tenor man and a clarinet guy. He was very good. I took them off to a head. Very fine. What kind of dancing did they do over there? Any jitterbugs? Oh yeah. Them young people. That's right. I don't know if there was any sort of western kind or Mexican style. Or anything else. Or anything else. I did. I did. I did.
I did.
